evidence.requirement: Use deep packet dissection for PCAP parsing; Scapy is recommended because it correctly handles VLAN tags, tunnels, and nested encapsulations that affect protocol counts and derived metrics.
Compute protocol and IP-related metrics with IPv4-specific rules: ARP is not IP, IPv6 is excluded from IP-related metrics, and only TCP/UDP packets contribute ports and 5-tuple flows.
Packets-per-minute statistics use 60-second buckets anchored to capture start with bucket index floor((timestamp - start_time) / 60), then take avg/max/min over bucket counts.
Entropy metrics use Shannon entropy over observed frequencies; IP entropy is over IPv4 packet source/destination IPs, and port entropy is over all TCP+UDP source/destination ports together.
Directed graph metrics use distinct IPs as nodes and unique directed (src_ip, dst_ip) pairs as edges; density is num_edges / (num_nodes * (num_nodes - 1)) with 0 when num_nodes < 2.
IAT metrics are computed from all packets sorted by timestamp; variance is population variance, CV is std/mean, and CV below about 0.5 indicates highly regular beacon-like traffic.
PCR uses full-frame bytes on IP-layer packets with PCR = (sent - recv) / (sent + recv); producer threshold is > 0.2 and consumer threshold is < -0.2.
Flows are distinct 5-tuples (src_ip, dst_ip, src_port, dst_port, protocol) for TCP/UDP only; bidirectional flows are counted once per forward/reverse pair.

Analysis flags are based on qualitative intrusion-detection guidance from computed metrics: port scanning requires converging evidence from a single source (high destination-port diversity/entropy, high SYN-only or half-open behavior, many unique destination ports); DoS is indicated by an extraordinary max-versus-average packet-rate spike; beaconing is indicated by unusually regular inter-arrival timing.

Ioctl numbers are encoded from direction, size, type, and number, and `struct timeval` changes size between 64-bit and 32-bit Linux, so timeval-based ppdev ioctls have architecture-dependent numeric values.
